item.title: Chinese women honored at UN exemplify power of women in rural revitalization
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Chinese women honored at UN exemplify power of women in rural revitalization Qu Dongyu, director-general of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), awards Chinese desertification fighter Yin Yuzhen (right) at the headquarters of the FAO in Rome, Italy. (Photo courtesy of the FAO's WeChat account) Recently, applause filled the Plenary Hall at the headquarters of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) in Rome, Italy, as Chinese women were honored for their achievements. A short documentary played on the giant screen, telling the story of a woman who has spent more than 40 years fighting desertification. When Yin Yuzhen, the film's protagonist, stepped onto the stage to receive her award, the audience rose to its feet in applause. Ronald Sakolsky, an American friend of Yin's who had traveled to Rome for the occasion, was clearly moved. Choking back tears, he praised Yin's unwavering dedication and called on everyone to plant a tree and work together to protect the environment. The emotional moment unfolded at a ceremony honoring the FAO's 100 Women Heroes in Agrifood Systems and Rural Development. Of the 609 nominees from 131 FAO member countries, 100 were selected for the honor. Three Chinese women -- Yin Yuzhen, Dong Minfang, and Yu Jinxiu -- made the list, giving China the highest number of honorees of any country. Each woman has advanced rural development through distinct pathways. For more than 40 years, Yin has worked tirelessly to halt sand encroachment in the Mu Us Desert in the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. Dong Minfang left a lucrative urban career to return to her hometown, where she has championed grain production, promoted agricultural mechanization, and boosted smallholder incomes. Yu Jinxiu has dedicated over two decades to promoting Qichun moxibustion therapy -- a nationally recognized intangible cultural heritage -- training more than 30,000 practitioners and expanding the local mugwort industry to create employment opportunities for women, people with disabilities, and other underserved groups. Though their methods differ, the three share a common mission: restoring degraded land, strengthening food security, and uplifting communities through perseverance and innovation. At the ceremony, FAO director-general Qu Dongyu noted that women play a critical role across agrifood systems, from ensuring food security and managing natural resources to advancing rural development and strengthening community resilience. Across China, the vital role women play in agriculture and rural development is reflected in countless real-life stories. Women have been both a key focus of China's poverty alleviation efforts and a driving force in advancing rural revitalization. They account for roughly half of the nearly 100 million people lifted out of poverty in China. A villager displays handmade baskets at a common prosperity workshop in Matou village, Xin'an county, Luoyang, central China's Henan province. (Photo/Zhang Guanghui) According to data from the All-China Women's Federation, women accounted for more than half of those engaged in family farming in 2023. They spent more time on average each year working in their own agricultural operations than men did. Their tireless work in the fields underscores the essential role women play in rural development. These outcomes have been supported by targeted institutional measures. By the end of 2020, 10.21 million impoverished women and rural female leaders had completed vocational skills training. Over five million women escaped poverty through initiatives ranging from crop cultivation and livestock rearing to handicrafts, domestic services, and e-commerce. Over 450 billion yuan (about $67.48 billion) in guaranteed microloans and poverty-alleviation microcredit had been disbursed to women in need and 8.7 million impoverished women had seen their income increased through entrepreneurship. Countless rural women have helped combat desertification through afforestation, secured livelihoods through farming, and built enterprises in agricultural processing. In transforming themselves from economically disadvantaged villagers into catalysts of rural prosperity, they have not only improved their own lives but also generated enduring momentum for sustainable rural development. The Outline for Women's Development in China (2021-2030) calls for further efforts to improve rural women's skills and capabilities and support their participation in agricultural and rural modernization. As supporting policies are put into practice, the protection of rural women's rights and interests continues to be strengthened. The achievements of rural Chinese women are also gaining recognition internationally. They bring the knowledge and experience gained from the field and farmyards to the international stage, offering the world a firsthand glimpse of China's efforts toward poverty alleviation and rural revitalization. Farmers harvest bamboo fungus in Shaojia village, Yongfeng county, Ji'an, east China's Jiangxi province. (Photo/Yuan Xuebin) On the international stage, they share not only China's stories, but also proven approaches that other developing countries can learn from and adapt, giving China's grassroots solutions a wider reach and greater resonance in global development. The recognition the three Chinese women received at the UN was not only a personal honor, but also a testament to the contributions of countless rural women across China who are deeply rooted in their communities. Across China's vast rural landscape, women continue to make their mark, building on the achievements of those before them and opening new chapters in the story of rural women in China. item.title: Protocol upgrading China-Peru FTA takes effect
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Protocol upgrading China-Peru FTA takes effect BEIJING, Nov. 1 (Xinhua) -- The protocol upgrading the China-Peru free trade agreement (FTA) took effect on Sunday, according to China's Ministry of Commerce (MOC). China and Peru launched negotiations on the upgrade in November 2018 and signed the protocol on Nov. 14, 2024. The original FTA was signed in 2009 and took effect in 2010. The protocol improves seven existing chapters of the original FTA, covering rules of origin, customs procedures and trade facilitation, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, intellectual property rights, trade in services, temporary entry of business personnel, and investment, the MOC said in an online statement. The protocol also adds five new chapters on standards and conformity assessment cooperation, competition policy, e-commerce, global supply chains, and environment and trade. The two sides also set out future provisions for negotiations on negative lists for trade in services and investment, aimed at further raising openness in these areas, according to the statement. The China-Peru FTA was the first comprehensive free trade agreement China signed with a Latin American country. China is Peru's largest trading partner, largest export market and largest source of imports, while Peru is China's fourth-largest trading partner in Latin America and an important investment destination, said an MOC official. Under the protocol, the new chapter on global supply chains encourages multimodal transport and the development of foreign trade logistics corridors and infrastructure, an innovative arrangement that signals the two countries' commitment to keeping supply chains stable and unimpeded. The chapter on standards and conformity assessment cooperation establishes a dedicated cooperation mechanism and sets out an intended cooperation list, creating a platform for mutual recognition of standards that is expected to reduce trade costs for enterprises. The two sides agreed to launch negotiations on negative lists for trade in services and investment within two years after the protocol takes effect, in a bid to further raise the level of openness in these areas and continue to tap the potential of bilateral trade and investment, the official added. Since the original FTA came into force in 2010, it has played an important role in promoting bilateral economic and trade cooperation. Two-way trade rose from 6.4 billion U.S. dollars in 2009 to 50.4 billion U.S. dollars in 2025, an increase of nearly seven times, official data show. The protocol is expected to help tap further opportunities for bilateral trade and investment cooperation, provide a better business environment for enterprises of both countries and inject new vitality into bilateral economic and trade relations, the MOC said. item.title: China's logistics sees improved performance as industrial upgrades support growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
China's logistics sees improved performance as industrial upgrades support growth BEIJING, Nov. 1 (Xinhua) -- China's logistics demand maintained steady growth in the first three quarters of the year, supported by industrial upgrading and resilient high-end manufacturing, official data showed Sunday. The total value of national social logistics reached 280 trillion yuan (about 41.7 trillion U.S. dollars) in the January-September period, up 4.9 percent year on year, according to data from the China Federation of Logistics and Purchasing. In the first three quarters, the value of industrial goods logistics rose 5.3 percent year on year, contributing 78 percent to the growth of the total. Within this growth, equipment manufacturing and high-tech manufacturing played a prominent leading role, with their shares rising to 37.6 percent and 18.3 percent, respectively, according to the federation. Logistics volumes for new products such as smart wristbands, 3D printing equipment and sensors surged 77.1 percent, 62.5 percent and 16.4 percent year on year, respectively, highlighting an accelerated shift toward new and upgraded industrial logistics demand, the data showed. From January to September, the total cost of social logistics reached 14.8 trillion yuan, up 4.2 percent year on year. The ratio of total social logistics costs to GDP stood at 13.8 percent, down 0.2 percentage points from the same period last year. "The dividends of logistics cost reduction continue to be released to the real economy," said Liu Yuhang, chief engineer of the federation. Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, Liu said that with the arrival of the e-commerce peak season and the year-end production rush, logistics demand is expected to be released in a concentrated manner. High-quality logistics development will provide strong support for the recovery of the real economy and the achievement of the full-year economic and social development goals, he said. item.title: China's marriage registration innovations boost the "sweet economy"
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
China's marriage registration innovations boost the "sweet economy" A new couple register for their marriage at a marriage registration site inside an amusement park in Suzhou, east China's Jiangsu Province on April 21, 2025. (Xinhua/He Leijing) * China has allowed couples to complete marriage registration at any qualified civil affairs registry nationwide, making it easier for them to combine registration with travel. * Local governments are improving public services for newlyweds, including premarital health checks, marriage-related legal awareness campaigns and wedding consumption vouchers. * By the end of 2025, China had established 1,330 outdoor sites for certificate presentation and 525 marriage registration sites in parks and other landmark locations. NANJING, Nov. 1 (Xinhua) -- Since China removed the requirement that couples register their marriages in the locality of their household registration, local authorities across the country have been exploring new venues and services to make the process more personalized and memorable. From tourist destinations to football stadiums, music festivals and university campuses, young couples are choosing venues of marriage registration that reflect their interests and love stories. Also contributing to this trend is the growth of China's wedding industry and a range of government measures to support marriage, childbirth and child-rearing. A new couple take part in a group wedding ceremony on boats in Nanjing, east China's Jiangsu Province, Oct. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/He Leijing) ROMANTIC MOMENT As a football fan, Wu Jingyu had never imagined that she and her would-be husband would register their marriage outside a football stadium during a match, exchanging vows and receiving their marriage certificate with the roar of the crowd in the background. "It was truly unforgettable. The passion of watching football blended with the joy and romance of getting married," Wu said, recalling the couple's emotional moment outside the home stadium at a recent Jiangsu Football City League match in the city of Wuxi, east China's Jiangsu Province. A photo wall and red ceremonial platform had been set up outside the stadium as a temporary marriage registration venue. Surrounded by cheering fans and family members, couples completed their formalities in a setting far removed from the conventional government service hall. Such arrangements are emerging across China as local authorities seek to meet the preferences of younger couples and give marriage registration a greater sense of occasion. In Nanjing, a city with around 2,500 years of recorded history in Jiangsu, couples interested in traditional culture can wear Han-style wedding robes and phoenix crowns, along with traditional makeup, for their registration ceremony. Other cities have incorporated marriage registration into music festivals, while some universities have organized group wedding ceremonies for alumni returning to their campuses. By the end of 2025, China had established 1,330 outdoor sites for certificate presentation and 525 marriage registration sites in parks and other landmark locations, according to the Ministry of Civil Affairs. "Younger Chinese are exercising greater autonomy in their views on love and marriage," said Zhou Yongbo, a professor at Soochow University in Jiangsu. "They value not only the marriage certificate but also a personalized experience, a sense of ceremony and memories they can cherish." A couple hold a destination wedding in Dali Bai Autonomous Prefecture, southwest China's Yunnan Province, May 10, 2025. (Xinhua) THE "SWEET ECONOMY" Since May 2025, China has allowed couples to complete marriage registration at any qualified civil affairs registry nationwide, making it easier for them to combine registration with travel. In Lijiang, southwest China's Yunnan Province, a couple exchanged vows in front of the snow-capped Yulong Snow Mountain, framed by a heart-shaped arch of white roses. This province's tourism and cut-flower industries give it natural advantages as a destination-wedding choice, and local scenic areas and wedding companies have moved quickly to build a mature industry. Yang Libin, head of a wedding planning company in Yunnan with over a decade of experience, began focusing on customized destination weddings in 2025. His team uses questionnaires and consultations to learn about couples' stories and preferences before selecting venues and designing ceremonies. "Professional services should improve the couples' experience and make every wedding unique," Yang said. In the first year after their shift of focus, his company organized more than 280 destination weddings. The wedding photography industry is another major part of the "sweet economy." In Lijiang, industry associations have introduced service standards covering makeup, clothing, photo production and after-sales support. Packages costing around 10,000 yuan (about 1,500 U.S. dollars) can include costumes, makeup, private transport and accommodation. By integrating photography, ceremonies and honeymoon travel, Lijiang attracted more than 140,000 couples in 2025, with its wedding industry market exceeding 1.1 billion yuan. In Dali, another popular Yunnan destination, businesses have developed over 30 wedding settings, including lakeside lawns and traditional Bai ethnic courtyards, drawing on the area's Cangshan Mountain and Erhai Lake. Wang Yu, a groom from Hebei Province in north China, and his wife held their ceremony in the morning and took wedding photos near Erhai Lake in the afternoon, while relatives and friends visited nearby attractions. "There were no complicated formalities, and we could combine getting married with traveling. It has been a great experience." A staff member provides marriage counseling service for a new couple at a local civil affairs department in Nanjing, east China's Jiangsu Province on Feb. 14, 2026. (Xinhua/He Leijing) IMPROVED PUBLIC SERVICES While simplifying registration procedures, local governments are also improving services for newlyweds. In Haidian District of Beijing, for example, its maternal and child health care hospital has set up a premarital health center inside the district's marriage registration office. Newlyweds can complete a premarital health check and marriage registration in the same building and on the same day. In Chengdu, capital of southwest China's Sichuan Province, a team from the local court has worked with marriage registration offices on multiple occasions during peak registration periods, giving newlyweds legal handbooks on marriage and family, Civil Code brochures, and briefings on spousal rights, joint property and family dispute resolution. This effort is part of a broader push to embed legal education into the registration process. Many localities have even introduced marriage incentives and wedding consumption vouchers to help newlyweds manage expenses. Also, many provincial-level regions have extended marriage leave, with the longest reaching 30 days. Local governments are seeking to link the development of the "sweet economy" with efforts to create a more supportive environment for marriage, childbirth and child-rearing. In 2025, China introduced 23 measures to support childbirth and child-rearing. Multiple regions have made childbirth-related medical expenses largely or entirely free for families, while Jiangsu has introduced childcare service vouchers. Zhou added that localities are pairing the new registration settings with premarital education and legal consultation, which helps young people understand the rights and obligations of marriage and avoid registering on impulse. "The business of romance is closely connected to people's aspirations for a better life," he said. "As society places greater emphasis on creating a family-friendly environment, preserving that sweetness requires continued innovation in public services." Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics opens in historic first for Africa
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics opens in historic first for Africa Photo shows the Olympic rings during the opening ceremony of the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, Oct. 31, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Wei) DAKAR, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- The Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games (YOG) opened on Saturday, marking the first time an Olympic event has been held on African soil. The opening ceremony took place at the 55,000-seat Abdoulaye Wade Stadium in Diamniadio, a new city located 30 km from Senegal's capital of Dakar. According to the organizing committee, Khady Niang, the ceremony director, said the show allows Africa to "tell the world who we are, where we come from and where we want to go." The two-hour show started at 6:30 p.m. local time, marked by the arrival of International Olympic Committee President Kirsty Coventry and Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye. Following the parade of athletes, the spotlight turned to a story of three generations passing the baton from one to the next: Alkebulan, the mother, represented the values of ancestral Africa; her son, Keb, embodied Africa today; and Sitoe, a young Senegalese girl, symbolized hope for the future. The opening act paid tribute to the Africa of the past, immediately electrifying the crowd as Alkebulan rode into the arena on horseback. Iconic instruments, including the sabar, the tama (talking drum) and the djembe, introduced the continent's rich musical heritage, while traditional attire from Mali, Ghana, Senegal and South Africa showcased the diversity of African cultural traditions. The momentum built with performances of Senegal's traditional faux-lion dance and wrestlers' dance, culminating in a finale in which 360 dancers came together to form the map of Africa. In the second act, Keb arrived on a motorcycle in a scene inspired by the Senegalese film Touki Bouki. He led Sitoe and the spectators into the world of contemporary African art, striking a chord with younger generations. As Keb and Sitoe strolled through the streets, a series of artistic performances featuring live painting, music, dance and hip-hop brought the scene to life. The festivities were followed by the parade of flags representing the participating national Olympic committees, with Greece and the Refugee Olympic Team leading the procession and host nation Senegal bringing up the rear. "For years, we have been talking about this moment -- the first Olympic sporting event on African soil and now here we are. This historic moment is for Senegal, for Africa, for our entire Olympic movement, and to all of our young amazing athletes," Coventry said in her speech. "This is the Africa that I am so proud and so excited for the world to experience," she added, voicing hope for young talents to "believe in yourselves, to dream big and to do things you never thought were possible." After Senegalese President Faye officially declared the fourth Summer Youth Olympic Games open, the stadium erupted in vibrant Afrobeats music. The celebration continued with sports demonstrations, a choreographed formation of the Olympic rings and the Dakar 2026 emblem, the Olympic anthem, the raising of the Olympic flag and the solemn reading of the Youth Olympic oath. The much-anticipated lighting of the Olympic cauldron came last. Senegalese fencer Abdourahmane Marieme Sy, 17, and judoka Aicha Diop, 15, jointly carried the final torch, receiving the flame from canoeist Yves Bourhis, triple jumper Sally Sarr and Amadou Dia Ba, Senegal's first and, to date, only Olympic medalist. As the Olympic cauldron was lit, dancers wearing masks and futuristic costumes created a pathway for an Afrofuturism-inspired fashion show. The act also featured a standout performance by a 12-year-old drummer whose solo drew loud applause. At 8:30 p.m., the performers took their final bow, bringing the ceremony to a jubilant close. Held in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly from Oct. 31 to Nov. 13, the fourth edition of the YOG will bring together more than 2,600 athletes from over 200 delegations. A total of 25 sports will feature on the official competition program, alongside 10 engagement sports. Dakar 2026 will also feature the Youth Olympic debuts of wushu, baseball5 and skateboarding, as well as the Refugee Olympic Team's historic first appearance at the Games. China has sent 66 athletes to compete in 21 sports at the Dakar Youth Olympics. Wushu athlete Lin Yilei and swimmer Chang Mohan, both 15, were named China's flagbearers for the opening ceremony. item.title: China's "porcelain capital" wins Global Award for Sustainable Development in Cities
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
China's "porcelain capital" wins Global Award for Sustainable Development in Cities This file photo shows a view of the Taoyangli Historical and Cultural Block in Jingdezhen, east China's Jiangxi Province. (Xinhua) FUZHOU, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- The global observance of 2026 World Cities Day was held on Saturday in east China's Fuzhou, with five cities, including China's "porcelain capital" Jingdezhen, honored with the fourth-cycle Global Award for Sustainable Development in Cities, also known as the Shanghai Award. The event runs from Oct. 31 to Nov. 2. Apart from Jingdezhen, the other four recipients of the Shanghai Award, which recognizes cities for achievements in sustainable urban development, are Addis Ababa in Ethiopia, Santiago de Cali in Colombia, Istanbul in Türkiye, and Katowice in Poland. The event brings together senior United Nations officials alongside representatives from national governments, local authorities, international organizations, academic institutions, the private sector, and community networks to share best practices and advance practical solutions to common urban challenges. In December 2013, the 68th United Nations General Assembly adopted a resolution designating Oct. 31 as World Cities Day starting in 2014. It was the first international day proposed by the Chinese government at the United Nations. Ceramic culture has long been an ideal medium for cross-civilization dialogue. As a cornerstone commodity of the ancient Silk Road, Jingdezhen porcelain was a defining cultural symbol, through which the world came to know China and China reached out to the world. Building on this legacy, Jingdezhen has embraced a model of development that combines cultural preservation with creative renewal. Former porcelain factories have been reimagined as cultural and creative districts, old streets are lined with ceramic-themed installations, and historic neighborhoods have been carefully preserved and revitalized. The city is home to more than 3,200 inheritors of intangible cultural heritage in ceramic craftsmanship. It has also been named in the UNESCO Creative Cities Network as a City of Crafts and Folk Art. Jingdezhen's recognition is just one example of China's broader urban renewal efforts. Urban renewal also holds huge potential for investment and consumption. China has set a target of renovating 1,500 old streets and factory compounds from 2026 to 2030, bringing in new industries and business models to inject fresh momentum into urban development. "Converting old streets and factory sites into cultural and creative districts drives growth in dining, retail and entertainment," said Yan Yuejin, deputy director of the E-house China R&D Institute.
